locator: Section XXII. DISPUTE RESOLUTION, E. Arbitration
quote: In the event the parties fail to resolve their dispute through negotiation and mediation, then either party may serve a written demand on the other for arbitration and the dispute shall be resolved through arbitration at a neutral location.
current_summary: After written notice the State and Tribe meet within 30 days, and if the dispute is unresolved after 90 days either party may pursue any otherwise available remedy, with mediation or arbitration only by mutual agreement.
proposed_summary: After written notice the State and Tribe meet within 10 days, then must go through non-binding mediation (at least two sessions) before either may demand binding arbitration before a single arbitrator, with the United States District Court handling actions to compel arbitration or confirm an award and other relief reserved to court.
differences: The summary sets a 30-day meeting period and makes mediation and arbitration available only by mutual agreement, but the clause sets a 10-day meeting and makes mediation and then arbitration required steps.
note: 2003 Amendments replaced Section XXII of the 1991 compact in its entirety (item 27 of the amendments). Sec. XXII.F/G also give court jurisdiction in federal district court for certain Sections and for provisional relief.

locator: DISPUTE RESOLUTION; B. Dispute Resolution Methods. (1. Good Faith Negotiations; 2. Mediation; 3. Arbitration)
quote: The parties shall meet and confer in a good faith attempt to resolve the dispute through negotiation not later than ten (10), days from receipt of the notice.
current_summary: Disputes start with written notice and a meet-and-confer within 20 business days; if unresolved, the parties may by agreement use formal mediation, may by mutual agreement use arbitration, and a party dissatisfied with mediation may seek judicial resolution.
proposed_summary: After written notice the parties meet and confer within ten days; if the dispute is not resolved within twenty days of the first meeting either party may seek mediation, and if no mediator can be agreed either party may seek arbitration under the Judicial Arbitration Management Service (JAMS) of Seattle, whose decision is final and unappealable only if the parties so agree in writing beforehand or the compact specifically says so, and is otherwise reviewable de novo by a federal district judge.
differences: The summary gives a 20-business-day meet-and-confer period (the clause says ten days after notice), says mediation and arbitration happen only by agreement (the clause lets either party seek them), and does not mention arbitration before JAMS, while judicial review in the clause applies to arbitration awards rather than to mediation.
note: 1995 compact's Section XII governs. Later amendments (1998, 2004, 2007 Appendix X2, 2015, 2021, 2026) do not replace it: 2007 text has its own TLS dispute section 17, 2015 adds an addendum dispute clause that refers back to the compact, and the 2026 Fifth Amendment text concerns facilities and appendices. The 2021 document is a memorandum of understanding and the 1999 file is OCR-garbled, so edits there cannot be fully excluded.

quote: If the dispute is not resolved to the satisfaction of the parties after the first meeting, either party may seek to have the dispute resolved by an arbitrator in accordance with this section, but neither party shall be required to agree to submit to arbitration.
current_summary: The parties exchange written notice and a written response within 15 days and must meet and confer within 30 days; disputes still unresolved may be taken to the United States District Court (or a state court if federal jurisdiction is lacking) for injunctive, declaratory or specific-performance relief only, under a limited waiver of sovereign immunity, and mediation or other methods may be used by mutual agreement.
proposed_summary: The parties exchange written notice and a written response within 15 days and must meet and confer within 30 days; if unresolved either party may seek arbitration before a JAMS arbitrator under JAMS Comprehensive Arbitration, with an optional JAMS appeal, though neither is required to agree to arbitrate, and disputes not resolved by arbitration or other agreed means may go to the United States District Court (or a state court if the federal court lacks jurisdiction) for injunctive, declaratory or specific-performance relief only, under a limited waiver of sovereign immunity.
differences: The summary leaves out the optional arbitration step: after the first meeting either party may seek arbitration before a JAMS arbitrator (neither must agree), and court action is for disputes not resolved by arbitration or other agreed means.
note: The 2017 Deemed Approved compact (133 pp.) governs. The 2018-01-22 document (9 pp.) is the Interior letter on a 2017 amendment (hotel/Sec. 4.2 and related); it refers to the Sec. 13.0 process but does not rewrite it.

nation: Zuni Tribe of the Zuni Reservation, New Mexico
governing_document: {"title": "Zuni Tribe Tribal State Gaming Compact", "date": "2021-05-24", "link": "https://www.bia.gov/sites/default/files/dup/assets/as-ia/oig/pdf/508%20Compliant%202021.05.24%20Zuni%20Tribe%20Tribal%20State%20Gaming%20Compact.pdf"}
locator: SECTION 15. DISPUTE RESOLUTION, (c)(2) Arbitrators.
quote: Unless the parties agree in writing to the appointment of a single arbitrator, the arbitration shall be conducted before a panel of three (3) arbitrators.
current_summary: Either party may serve written notice of non-compliance or an interpretation dispute, after which agency heads and then designated tribal and gubernatorial representatives negotiate; if unresolved within 30 days, either party may request non-binding mediation under CPR Institute for Dispute Resolution procedures and may then demand binding arbitration under CPR rules before three arbitrators unless both agree to one.
differences: Leaves out that injunctive relief may still be sought in a court of competent jurisdiction in aid of arbitration or to enforce an award, that judgment on an award may be entered in any competent court, that the arbitrators cannot award money damages, and that Sec. 15 is not a waiver of sovereign immunity; the first negotiation step is a 10-day meeting of agency heads.
note: Governing clause is Sec. 15 of the 2021 Amended and Restated compact (80 pp.), identical across the Arizona tribes. The 2022 amendment (20 pp.) only says disputes under it use Sec. 15 and does not rewrite it.

locator: SECTION 7. Dispute Resolution., A.3
quote: Unless the pai1ies agree in writing to the appointment of a single arbitrator, or as otherwise provided below, the arbitration shall be conducted before a panel of three (3) arbitrators.
current_summary: Within two years of a discovered violation a party serves written notice, may serve a notice to cease the challenged activity after 20 days, and either side may then invoke binding arbitration before three attorney arbitrators (the third chosen by the American Arbitration Association if needed), with awards enforceable by injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction.
differences: The summary says either side may invoke arbitration after the 20-day period; the clause lets the complaining party serve a notice to cease the activity, and the responding party then may stop the activity or invoke arbitration (the complaining party invokes it only if the responding party does neither within 10 days). It also leaves out that a single arbitrator may be agreed or may proceed alone if the responding party fails to appoint, and that Sec. 7 is not a waiver of sovereign immunity.
